correctness.rationale: For a retained cell the induced degree is m+n−2−r_i−c_j, where r_i and c_j count deletions from its row and column. Mixed parity gives odd degree on the full board, and an empty 1×1 remainder is vacuously odd. Otherwise fewer than m deletions leave an untouched row-column intersection, while deleting a full column attains m deletions. At equality for m<n an untouched column forces every row to be hit, and on a square the same obstruction forces all rows or all columns to be hit. With one deletion per row, any nonfull column must have even deletion count. This includes all columns if m is even, while if m is odd some full column must account for the entire odd deletion count. The converse is the same degree test. The row and column families on a square cannot overlap when m≥2 because a permutation matrix of deletions gives retained cells even degree. Counting labelled maps by even fibre sizes gives the cosh coefficient; the degree-r term at fixed m=2r comes solely from r fibres of size two, yielding (2r−1)!! times the falling factorial (n)_r. This verifies the stated cases and asymptotics.
residual_risks: Finite checks illustrate the proof; the theorem counts labelled rather than symmetry-quotiented sets and concerns maximum cardinality only.

evidence: At the credited optimum of mn−m for same-parity dimensions, an untouched row and column would form a selected cell whose selected row and column sums have the same parity, excluded by the primary parity-block characterization.

Thus the m deletions hit all rows if m<n, and all rows or all columns on a square. After orienting them to hit rows, each row has one deletion and parity opposite to the original row. Every nonfull column must then retain the original column parity, so it has an even fibre. When m is odd the odd total forces one full column. The two square families overlap only in the singleton case, since an overlapping permutation matrix violates the parity-block rule on any retained cell.
The fixed-width growth term counts the maximal possible number of occupied even fibres, necessarily pairs.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The parity-block characterization specializes directly to the actual maximizing sets, not just to a numerical match. Multinomial fibre counting and taking the largest number of pairs do not establish a substantively different remaining theorem.

value.rationale: A truly unrecorded equality classification for this natural graph family would be useful: a scalar optimum alone does not encode the labelled extremizers. Here the exact full polynomial and its structural parity-block theorem are already available. The simplified top coefficient, its square duplication and the fixed-width leading power follow from the forced minimum-deletion fibres by short specialization. No distinct nonroutine invariant or structural gap is left for a valuable repair.
residual_risks: The judgment concerns the incremental claim against verified coverage, not the utility of closed forms or equality classifications generally.
